exposure: elevated polygenic burden for Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD)
outcome: later diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD)
cohort: The study included 1263 infants, approximately 50% of whom subsequently developed ASD, with DNA isolated from archived blood spots taken shortly after birth.
finding: A significant association was found between elevated polygenic burden for autism and specific neonatal methylomic variation, specifically a -0.14% mean increase in DNA methylation at two CpG sites on chromosome 8 for each unit of elevated ASD polygenic risk score.
